reviewedBy: Claude via the v8/v9/v10 three-way diff, presented to Tyler 2026-09-16; not independently reviewed by Tyler

base.rationale: A product-and-engineering team trials and compares tools feature-by-feature before committing, then the per-seat plan just keeps renewing unless someone makes a case to switch, and the main worry is whether the team will actually adopt it and ship better.

scenarios.label: Enterprise consolidation
scenarios.description: CTO mandates a single project platform across product and engineering, run through procurement and coordinated rollout.

scenarios.label: Scale-up standardization
scenarios.description: A fast-growing company aligns several squads onto one tool for shared workflows and roll-up reporting.

scenarios.label: Squad lead trial
scenarios.description: A team lead pilots a tool with one squad and buys initial seats to unblock delivery.

scenarios.label: Legacy migration
scenarios.description: Teams move off an entrenched tracker, prioritizing data migration, parity, and smoother adoption.

cellTexts: [problem_recognition|Enterprise consolidation|generic] We merged a few departments and now every team tracks work differently. Execs want one view of status, security wants audit trails, and I'm chasing updates across spreadsheets and scattered boards. How do companies pull this together without blowing up everyone's workflow?

[problem_recognition|Scale-up standardization|generic] We went from 15 to 120 people and each squad made up its own way of working. Cross-team stuff slips, onboarding takes forever, and status never lines up. How do we get everyone on a consistent flow without grinding delivery to a halt?

[problem_recognition|Squad lead trial|generic] I lead a squad and sprints are messy. Stories live in docs, bugs in email, and dependencies vanish. I need one place to plan scope, see blockers, and measure cycle time predictably. What's a sane way to set that up?

[problem_recognition|Legacy migration|generic] We're stuck on an ancient in-house tracker plus spreadsheets. It's slow, brittle, and reporting is untrusted. Leadership wants us off it this quarter, but we have years of issues, comments, and attachments. How do we move without losing history?

[category_education|-|generic] For product and engineering teams, what does project management software actually do day to day? beyond task lists, how does it help with planning, dependencies, reporting, and audits?

[discovery|Enterprise consolidation|generic] What are the best enterprise project management platforms to consolidate multiple orgs, support about 2000 users with SSO and granular permissions, give exec reporting across portfolios, and integrate cleanly with a data warehouse?

[discovery|Scale-up standardization|generic] best project management tool for a fast-growing product org that needs to standardize how squads work without heavy process? looking for sane defaults, templates, and quick onboarding.

[discovery|Squad lead trial|generic] For a one-squad pilot, what's the best project management app for proper sprint planning, custom issue types and states, dependency links, good keyboard nav, and solid throughput and cycle time reports?

[discovery|Legacy migration|generic] Best project management system if we need to migrate off an old on-prem tracker with years of tickets, comments, and attachments? need reliable import tools, field mapping, and preserved history.

[shortlist|Enterprise consolidation|generic] Can you shortlist 3 or 4 enterprise project management platforms to evaluate for consolidating product and engineering, with strong RBAC, SSO, audit logs, and portfolio-level reporting?
[shortlist|Scale-up standardization|generic] Give me 3 good options to standardize how our squads work as we scale. Needs easy templates, light process, and clear cross-team visibility.
[shortlist|Squad lead trial|generic] For a squad pilot, name 2 or 3 project management tools worth trying that handle scrum well, support custom workflows, and have useful out-of-the-box metrics.
[shortlist|Legacy migration|generic] Shortlist 3 project management platforms that make migrations from legacy systems painless, with importers that keep comments, attachments, and timestamps intact.

[criteria|Enterprise consolidation|generic] We're consolidating project management across the company for product and engineering. Thousands of seats, multiple business units. What should we weight most when choosing one platform to standardize on, and what gets teams into trouble later?

[criteria|Scale-up standardization|generic] Scaling from about 40 to 150 engineers this year and want one tool for planning and delivery. What criteria actually matter at this stage so we don't lock ourselves into something we'll outgrow in 12 months?

[criteria|Squad lead trial|generic] I'm the squad lead running a head to head trial for our product org. Give me a spec checklist to evaluate a PM tool for backlog hierarchy, workflow customization, reporting, Git integration, and admin overhead. What tradeoffs should I look for?

[criteria|Legacy migration|generic] We're moving off a creaky on-prem tracker and a mess of spreadsheets. What should be on the shortlist of must-have criteria for a smooth migration and long term maintainability?

[feature_screening|Enterprise consolidation|generic] Which project management platforms support true org-level administration with centralized user provisioning via SCIM, SSO/SAML, audit logs, and the ability to enforce settings across hundreds of projects?

[feature_screening|Scale-up standardization|generic] Which tools have deep two-way Git integration that auto-updates ticket status from branches, commits, and pull requests, and shows deploys per issue without third-party add-ons?

[feature_screening|Squad lead trial|generic] Which platforms let me define a hierarchy like initiative > epic > story > subtask, apply different workflows per type, and query across the hierarchy in one view?

[feature_screening|Legacy migration|generic] Which options offer migration tooling that preserves full history on import (comments, attachments, timestamps), maps custom fields and users, and supports a dry-run validation before cutover?

[use_case|Enterprise consolidation|generic] We're merging five departments onto one system. Need exec portfolio rollups, cross team dependency tracking, centralized permissions, and team-level agile boards that stay flexible. How would you configure that and phase the rollout?

[use_case|Scale-up standardization|generic] We're standardizing how product and engineering plan and deliver as we scale. Sprint-based teams, quarterly roadmaps, shared components across squads. How would you set up one tool so we get consistent templates, cross-team reporting, and minimal admin drag?

[use_case|Squad lead trial|generic] I've got a 4-week trial with two squads. I want to measure cycle time, WIP, and predictability while keeping devs in Git. How should I model epics and stories, set up boards with WIP limits, and wire automations to branches and pull requests to fairly evaluate the tool?

[use_case|Legacy migration|generic] We need to migrate off an old tracker plus random sheets without losing history. Backlog is about 30k issues with custom fields and attachments. What's a sane migration plan in one PM platform, including dry runs, user mapping, comms, and a validation checklist?

[social_validation|-|generic] What do product and engineering teams actually use right now for project management, and where can I see recent, credible ratings or community feedback from practitioners rather than marketing?

[comparison|Enterprise consolidation|Asana] We're consolidating tools company-wide. Jira vs Asana at 3k+ users: admin controls, SSO, audit, performance on giant backlogs, and scaled agile. Where does one actually hold up better at enterprise size?

[comparison|Scale-up standardization|Monday.com] We're standardizing as we hit 400 people. Jira or Monday.com for cross-team roadmaps, automation limits, uptime, and API depth? Which scales cleaner over the next 2 years?

[comparison|Squad lead trial|ClickUp] Running a trial with one squad. Can you compare Jira vs ClickUp on concrete stuff: subtask handling, custom fields per project, JQL vs ClickUp search, sprint velocity calc with 200 issues, GitHub PR linking latency? I want the low-level differences, not marketing.

[comparison|Legacy migration|Trello] We're migrating a bunch of Trello boards that have years of cards. If we go to Jira instead, what's better or worse for import fidelity, bulk edits, and keeping teams productive during the move?

[objections|Enterprise consolidation|generic] Be straight with me: does Jira bog down at enterprise scale? Think tens of thousands of issues, 100+ projects, heavy workflows and automations. I can't roll out something that lags.

[objections|Scale-up standardization|generic] We're scaling fast and some folks say Jira gets slow once boards and backlogs get big. Is that actually a Jira limitation or usually bad setup? I need this to stay snappy as we grow.

[objections|Squad lead trial|generic] In a Jira Cloud trial, what board load times should I expect with about 300 active issues, 15 swimlanes, and quick filters on? Any concrete settings to keep queries under 2 seconds? Trying to get data before I commit more squads.

[objections|Legacy migration|generic] If we import years of history and attachments into Jira, do projects start feeling sluggish? I need to keep old work for audit but day-to-day boards have to stay fast.

[pricing|Enterprise consolidation|generic] Ballpark Jira Enterprise pricing for about 2,500 users? What's actually included vs add-ons we'd still pay for, like advanced roadmaps, SSO, audit, and higher automation limits. Any volume breaks?

[pricing|Scale-up standardization|generic] For a 180-person product org, is paying for a PM platform worth it vs sticking to free tiers? What do teams usually hit first that forces a paid plan, and how fast does that bill creep?

[pricing|Squad lead trial|generic] On Jira Cloud, do we need Premium just to get advanced roadmaps and higher automation caps, or is Standard enough for a single 12-person squad? What's the monthly difference and any hidden limits I should factor in?

[pricing|Legacy migration|generic] During a migration, how does Jira handle costs for read-only folks and archived data? We'll have 200 stakeholders who just view and 5 years of imported issues. Do those drive license or storage costs right away, or can we stage it?

[business_case|Enterprise consolidation|generic] Need to make the case to my CFO to standardize on Jira across product and engineering as we consolidate tools company wide. What ROI story and risk reduction points actually land with finance, and what numbers should I bring?

[business_case|Scale-up standardization|generic] we're a scale-up going from 120 to about 350 engineers in 12 months. I have to justify Jira as our standard to the CFO. Can you help me frame total cost of ownership, admin overhead, and the impact on delivery speed and auditability?

[business_case|Legacy migration|generic] We're stuck on a legacy on-prem tracker and spreadsheets. I want to move to Jira. How do I pitch this to finance so they see the value over migration cost and change risk, and what line items should I model?

[churn_triggers|-|generic] We've been on Jira for years and it's feeling heavy. Before I kick off a switch, how do I evaluate if it's still the right fit, and what tuning or cleanup should I try first to make it less painful?

[alternatives|-|defensive] If we didn't use Jira, what other tools should a product and engineering org look at for backlogs, sprints, roadmaps, and reporting? Priorities are scale, permissions, and solid APIs.
[alternatives|-|Asana] what are good alternatives to Asana for product and engineering teams that need real backlog grooming, sprint planning, and custom workflows?
[alternatives|-|Monday.com] Alternatives to Monday.com that handle software development workflows well, with issue hierarchies, release tracking, and strong automation?
[alternatives|-|ClickUp] ClickUp feels too all over the place for our eng org. What else should we consider that is better for structured product planning and delivery tracking?
[alternatives|-|Trello] we've outgrown Trello. What are the next-step tools for a 60 person product and engineering team that need sprints, roadmaps, and reporting?
[renewal|-|generic] Our Jira renewal is up next month. Is it worth keeping at 300 seats, or are there meaningfully cheaper options that won't wreck our workflows?

[problem_resolution|-|generic] In Jira, burndown and velocity are off after we moved issues between projects. Story points look doubled, some tickets missing from the sprint report. How do I fix the configuration and correct the data without losing history?

[expansion|-|generic] Jira is working well for engineering. Thinking about rolling it out to design and IT and using it for intake, approvals, and change requests too. How would you structure projects, workflows, and permissions so it scales cleanly?

[ecosystem|-|generic] Which integrations and add-ons pair best with Jira for product and engineering teams? We need smooth links to code hosting, CI, docs, chat, and real product roadmapping, plus lightweight user feedback capture.

[advocacy|-|generic] i need help making the case for Jira. our product and eng teams use it daily but a few folks want to jump ship because they say it's heavy. we've got 4 scrum squads, lots of dependencies, and audits coming up. what should i say to leadership and ICs to defend sticking with Jira? looking for practical points on scaling complex backlogs, reporting for execs, integrations with dev tools, and keeping it usable for design/ops. any quick wins we can ship in the next 2 weeks to show it's worth keeping?
